questions.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=-5$ and ${\mu }_{2}=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}-{X}_{2}] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}]-\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & ={\mu }_{1}-{\mu }_{2} \\  & =-5-2 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=3,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=7,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[{X}_{1}-{X}_{2}] \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot 3+(-1)^{2}\cdot 7+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =3+7+4 \\  & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(-7,14).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y=-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=-1$ and ${\mu }_{2}=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}] \\  & =-3\text{E}[{X}_{1}]+2\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & =-3\cdot {\mu }_{1}+2\cdot {\mu }_{2} \\  & =-3\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 4 \\  & =3+8 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=5,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=3,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[-3{X}_{1}+2{X}_{2}] \\  & =(-3)^{2}\cdot 5+{2}^{2}\cdot 3+2\cdot (-3)\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =45+12-24 \\  & =33.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(11,33).
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y=-5{X}_{1}-4{X}_{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=1$ and ${\mu }_{2}=-1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[-5{X}_{1}-4{X}_{2}] \\  & =-5\text{E}[{X}_{1}]-4\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & =-5\cdot {\mu }_{1}-4\cdot {\mu }_{2} \\  & =-5\cdot 1-4\cdot (-1) \\  & =-5+4 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=3,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=2,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[-5{X}_{1}-4{X}_{2}] \\  & =(-5)^{2}\cdot 3+(-4)^{2}\cdot 2+2\cdot (-5)\cdot (-4)\cdot (-2) \\  & =75+32-80 \\  & =27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(-1,27).
$$

Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y=2{X}_{1}-{X}_{2}-{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =-2-1-4 \\  & =-7,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =14+4+7 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y∼N(-7,25).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(Y\le -2).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le -2) & =P(Z\le \frac{-2-(-7)}{\sqrt{25}}) \\  & =P(Z\le 1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\le 1) & =Φ(1).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(1)=0.8413.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\le 1)=0.8413.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\le -2)=0.8413.
$$

Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{k}]^{T}$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y={c}^{T}X={\sum }_{i=1}^{k}{c}_{i}{X}_{i}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y=2{X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+2{X}_{3},$ we have 

$$
c=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-2+0+2 \\  & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ 6 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =14+6+20 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
Y∼N(0,40).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(-6<Y\le 12).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-6<Y\le 12) & =P(\frac{-6-0}{\sqrt{40}}<Z\le \frac{12-0}{\sqrt{40}}) \\  & =P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90) & =P(Z\le 1.90)-P(Z\le -0.95) \\  & =Φ(1.90)-Φ(-0.95).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.95) & =0.8289 \\ Φ(1.90) & =0.9713\end{aligned}
$$

By the symmetry of the normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-0.95)=1-Φ(0.95)=1-0.8289=0.1711.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.95<Z\le 1.90)=0.9713-0.1711=0.8002.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(-6<Y\le 12)=0.8002.
$$
